title: Ribollita Tuscan Twice Boiled Soup

seo.title: Authentic Ribollita Recipe - Tuscan Twice-Boiled Soup
seo.metaDescription: Discover how to make authentic Ribollita, the hearty Tuscan twice-boiled soup. This traditional Italian recipe is packed with vegetables, beans, and stale bread for a comforting meal.

description: Ribollita is a quintessential Tuscan peasant soup, a hearty and comforting dish that truly embodies the Italian concept of cucina povera. This robust twice-boiled soup artfully combines seasonal vegetables, cannellini beans, and day-old bread, transforming humble ingredients into a rich and flavorful meal. It is a celebration of rustic Italian flavors, perfect for a satisfying and nourishing experience.

instructions.title: Prepare the Soffritto
instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté gently for about 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent, being careful not to brown them.

instructions.title: Add Garlic and Tomatoes
instructions.text: Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Simmer with Beans and Broth
instructions.text: Add the rinsed cannellini beans and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and let it cook for about 15 minutes, allowing the flavors to deepen.

instructions.title: Incorporate the Greens
instructions.text: Stir in the chopped black kale, shredded cabbage, and Swiss chard. Continue to simmer for another 10-15 minutes, or until all the greens are tender. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

instructions.title: Assemble and Twice Boil
instructions.text: Remove about half of the soup mixture from the pot and blend it roughly with an immersion blender, or mash it with a potato masher, then return it to the pot. Alternatively, you can blend about a third of the soup and then return. This creates a thicker texture. Layer the bottom of the pot with a third of the stale bread, then cover with a ladleful of the soup. Repeat layering with bread and soup until all ingredients are used, ending with a layer of soup. Gently press down.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Let the assembled soup rest for at least 30 minutes, or ideally for several hours or overnight in the refrigerator, allowing the bread to absorb the liquid and the flavors to fully develop. Before serving, gently reheat the soup over low heat, stirring carefully. Serve hot, drizzled with extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkle of freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano, if desired.

tips: For the most authentic Ribollita, use a good quality stale Tuscan bread (pane toscano), which is traditionally unsalted. If not available, any rustic, dense day-old bread will work best.
The twice-boiled aspect refers to the reheating of the soup, often the day after it is made, which allows the flavors to truly meld and deepen. Do not skip the resting period.
A generous drizzle of high-quality extra virgin olive oil just before serving is crucial for the authentic Tuscan taste and aroma. It adds a wonderful richness and peppery finish.
